_meta.model: naive-canopy counterfactual: build_envelope._rib and build_envelope._recaptured_sun reused UNCHANGED by import; only the height/reach/heading driver is replaced by a uniform constant. Injected via svf_deck=0 (openness_gate=1), which makes _rib's internal drive equal the passed `deficit` verbatim.

params.seed_note: no stochastic step in this engine; recorded for convention
params.fixed_directionality_note: constant across stations, so reach is fixed; 1.0 is the generator's maximum, giving the naive canopy the longest reach it can have at its drive — deliberately the generous choice
params.kg_per_m_note: assumed linear density, not a structural sizing

limitations: Same-primitive validation. Every variant is measured by the ray-caster that generated the field-driven form, so this is an internal-consistency comparison, not an independent one (IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md W3.1).
The recapture metric is winter-sun timesteps clear at the reach tip — a point measure at one height, not an irradiance integral over the deck.
The uniform variants are aimed by a single global heading. A naive designer could do better with a per-station rule that is still not the measured field; that intermediate control is not tested here.

a_equal_max_height.label: equal max height — 7.00 m rib at every station, reach fixed, heading fixed north
a_equal_max_height.deficit_vs_ribheight_r_note: null, not 0 — rib height is constant by construction, so the correlation is undefined (zero variance), not measured-and-found-absent. That undefinedness IS the counterfactual: a uniform canopy cannot track the field it ignores.

b_equal_member_length.label: equal total member length — 2869.1 m redistributed uniformly, reach fixed, heading fixed north
b_equal_member_length.solver: bisection on the uniform drive, 60 iterations, deterministic
b_equal_member_length.deficit_vs_ribheight_r_note: null, not 0 — constant rib height, zero variance, correlation undefined.
